lines: Progressive right arm swelling and discomfort
The patient is admitted to Hematology & Oncology for chemotherapy initiation following her recent Gynecologic Oncology encounter for suspected ovarian cancer recurrence.
Given her history of catheter-related upper extremity deep vein thrombosis, she presents with new right arm symptoms.
She had a peripherally inserted central catheter placed in her right arm two weeks ago for this purpose.
She reports a 3-day history of progressive right arm swelling and discomfort.

encounters.cc: presents to her oncologist for a routine follow-up

lines: She presents to her oncologist for a routine follow-up

This 68-year-old female with a history of stage III ovarian cancer diagnosed in 2020 and complicated by prior catheter-related upper extremity deep vein thrombosis returns for routine oncology follow-up.
She has been undergoing chemotherapy for the past 18 months, but recent imaging studies show progressive disease with multiple liver metastases and ascites.
She reports increasing fatigue, abdominal discomfort, and decreased appetite over the past month.
She denies any nausea, vomiting, or changes in bowel habits.
Her performance status has declined, and she is now mostly bedridden.

The patient is a 72-year-old woman with a longitudinal history notable for vulvar pruritus and burning consistent with lichen sclerosus since 2020, stage III ovarian cancer initially presenting with abdominal bloating and increased girth, and complicated by catheter-related upper extremity deep vein thrombosis.
She returns to the inpatient setting for management of pain and dyspnea.
She has been on chemotherapy for the past 18 months, but her disease has progressed, and she has decided to focus on comfort measures.
She reports a constant, dull ache in her abdomen, with intermittent sharp pains that she rates as 8 out of 10 in intensity.
She also experiences shortness of breath with minimal exertion.
The patient's family is at the bedside and expresses their wish for her to be as comfortable as possible in her remaining time.
